\section[la infancia]{la infancia — childhood}

\label{lesson:ES-C483-infancia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for fast, then the Spanish for the variety.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la infancia}
\textbf{la infancia} — \textquotedblleft{}childhood\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pasé la infancia en un pueblo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I spent my childhood in a village.}
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la costumbre]{la costumbre — the custom, the habit}

\label{lesson:ES-C483-costumbre}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the variety, then the Spanish for childhood.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la costumbre}
\textbf{la costumbre} — \textquotedblleft{}the custom, the habit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es costumbre comer tarde.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is the custom to eat late.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Tener la costumbre de} — to be in the habit of.

\section[acudir]{acudir — to go, to come (to a place or to someone for help)}

\label{lesson:ES-C483-acudir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the purpose, then the Spanish for the improvement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: acudir}
\textbf{acudir} — \textquotedblleft{}to go, to come (to a place or to someone for help)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Acuda a la oficina con su pasaporte.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Come to the office with your passport.}
\end{quote}

Notices use it where speech would use \emph{ir} or \emph{venir}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}
